conflicts.point: Whether upstream physical computing thresholds and lithography supply chain controls can effectively prevent catastrophic AI risks without creating insurmountable market monopolies.

positions.stance: National regulators and the UN must enforce upstream compute caps and lithography supply chain controls because open-weight models are unrecallable once released.
Compute thresholds and lithography access restrictions substitute software red tape with silicon foundry monopolies, protecting legacy conglomerates.

conflicts.point: Whether cryptographic verification methods and zero-knowledge proofs can successfully secure decentralized open-source AI models without relying on central authorities.

positions.stance: Cryptographic telemetry and zero-knowledge proofs enable independent developers to verify safety and training history trustlessly, rendering centralized gatekeepers obsolete.
Post-training safety methods and decentralized checks fail under pressure and lack permanent security against unconstrained model capabilities.

verdicts.conflict: Whether upstream physical computing thresholds and lithography supply chain controls can effectively prevent catastrophic AI risks without creating insurmountable market monopolies.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics offer a concrete analysis of how statutory machinery restrictions consolidate market power among incumbent firms. Safety advocates rely on abstract compute thresholds that lack robust enforcement mechanisms for decentralized hardware.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that upstream compute caps can be enforced without granting market monopolies to incumbent semiconductor fabricators.

verdicts.conflict: Whether cryptographic verification methods and zero-knowledge proofs can successfully secure decentralized open-source AI models without relying on central authorities.
verdicts.rationale: Safety advocates demonstrate that post-training safety filters fail under prompt optimization pressure. Accelerationists rely on theoretical zero-knowledge machine learning without empirical proof of scale against determined adversaries.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical demonstration that zero-knowledge proofs can permanently prevent adversarial prompt optimization on decentralized models without central oversight.
